policy: Consent-based (owner D22, ADR-0015, ADR-0017): TDflowMCP changes a coding agent's configuration only after the user approved the exact plan in TouchDesigner, and only for clients marked 'automatic' (Claude Code: one user-scope 'tdflow' entry with a headersHelper; Codex on Windows: one [mcp_servers.tdflow] table with http_headers_helper; the token stays in the OS-protected store). Other clients get a manual fallback: the token is referenced as ${TDFLOW_TOKEN} (or the client's own environment syntax) and never written into any file. 'verified' requires a recorded live test (docs/icm/validation-index.md).

mcp.config_file_note: Project scope: .mcp.json at the project root (shared via version control). User/local scope: ~/.claude.json via 'claude mcp add'. ${VAR} is expanded in 'headers'.

add_command.bash: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user tdflow {url} --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${TDFLOW_TOKEN}'
add_command.zsh: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user tdflow {url} --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${TDFLOW_TOKEN}'
add_command.powershell: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user tdflow {url} --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${TDFLOW_TOKEN}'

mcp.add_command_note: Single quotes keep ${TDFLOW_TOKEN} literal in bash, zsh and PowerShell, so the token itself is never stored. Documented form; the live test used the JSON form.

automatic.config: ~/.claude.json (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json), top-level mcpServers.tdflow (user scope: no project trust prompt)
automatic.mechanism: headersHelper: a fixed command that reads this project's token from the OS-protected store (Windows DPAPI file; macOS Keychain) for the project the listener announces; Claude Code runs it on each connection and again after a 401
shared_by: Claude Code VS Code extension (and other editor hosts of the extension)
automatic.windows_shell: cmd.exe (observed 2026-11-24: CLI 2.1.289 and VS Code extension 2.1.330)

mcp.config_file_note: ~/.codex/config.toml (shared by the Codex CLI, IDE extension and desktop app; CODEX_HOME). bearer_token_env_var names the variable that holds the token.

clients.facts_note: Vendor docs (learn.chatgpt.com: http_headers_helper is a 'string (command)' that prints a JSON object of header names and values, 'supported only for locally connected HTTP MCP servers'; explicit bearer tokens and OAuth credentials take precedence) and observation of the installed engines on Windows, 2026-11-25.
clients.manual_reason: automatic setup for Codex needs Windows and a recent Codex (tested: CLI 0.160.0, VS Code extension 26.1117 or newer); on Windows, update Codex and pulse Connect Agent again. Otherwise Codex reads its token from an environment variable when it starts

automatic.mechanism: http_headers_helper: the same fixed command, vault and listener proof as Claude Code's headersHelper; on any failure it exits with status 1 and prints nothing, so Codex sends no request
shared_by: Codex VS Code extension (and other editor hosts of the extension)
Codex desktop app (per the vendor documentation; not tested)
automatic.reload: chats started afterwards; a running Codex runs the helper again after a 401
automatic.windows_shell: cmd.exe /Q /D /C, reduced environment (observed 2026-11-25: CLI 0.160.0 and the extension's engine 0.171.0-alpha.13.2)
automatic.not_supported: Codex running in a remote or cloud execution environment; macOS and Linux (not observed)

mcp.config_file_note: ~/.cursor/mcp.json (all projects); restart Cursor or toggle the server after editing.

clients.manual_reason: Cursor reads its token from an environment variable when it starts

mcp.config_file_note: ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (Copilot user file, also the Copilot CLI's; COPILOT_HOME). The variable must be in VS Code's environment when it starts.

clients.manual_reason: Copilot reads its token from an environment variable VS Code has at start
clients.detect_note: Detected by the github.copilot* extension folder only ('code' on PATH says nothing about Copilot).

mcp.config_file_note: Any MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP and a custom Authorization header: server name tdflow, URL {url}, header Authorization: Bearer <token from the TDFLOW_TOKEN environment variable>. Follow your client's documentation.

clients.manual_reason: TDflowMCP cannot configure an unknown client

token_env.bash: read -rs TDFLOW_TOKEN && export TDFLOW_TOKEN   # paste the token, press Enter (not echoed, not in history)
token_env.zsh: read -rs TDFLOW_TOKEN && export TDFLOW_TOKEN   # paste the token, press Enter (not echoed, not in history)
token_env.powershell: $env:TDFLOW_TOKEN = [Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', (Read-Host -AsSecureString 'TDflowMCP token')).Password   # this terminal only; Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7

detect_policy: Auto detection is read-only: it looks the names in 'detect' up on PATH (shutil.which) and lists known extension and configuration folder names (connect.discover). It never runs them, never reads their configuration and never reports paths; a hit is a hint, not proof that the client works.
